text:
Sebastian Aho is now the Hurricanes' all-time leading goal scorer, passing the mark last week with his 323rd. A second-round pick in 2015, a Stanley Cup last spring, and a franchise record at 29: not a bad résumé for the 35th player taken in his draft.

His season is loud, too: 13 goals and 34 points in 25 games, 12 on the power play. Some of that will come back to earth. He's shooting 19.7%, well above the 14.5% our numbers think is his real level, and Carolina has scored 5.8 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. That's padding, and padding like that fades.

The engine underneath is real. The Canes get 60% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him 94th percentile among forwards for driving play last season, though he also plays with strong teammates. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flags one habit to watch: plenty of shot volume, fewer looks from the slot than you'd expect. If the bounces cool, our range still puts him at 84 to 109 points.
